\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Noise Contraction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.FiniteNoiseContraction
\section{Overview}
Two-valued vectors reduce weighted finite-noise contraction to a two-point estimate. Normalization and the extremal-vector result give the sharp inequality for every finite probability vector.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Grouping a two-valued weighted sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, let real weights satisfy $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $f:I\to\bbr$ take values in $\{a,b\}$, where $a,b\in\bbr$. For any $\varphi:\bbr\to\bbr$, setting $\gamma=\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i$ gives $\sum_iw_i\varphi(f_i)=\gamma\varphi(a)+(1-\gamma)\varphi(b)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mass of two nonconstant level sets]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_mass_dichotomy}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, and $0<\lambda\le w_i$ for every $i$. If $f:I\to\bbr$ takes values in $\{a,b\}$, then either $f$ is identically $a$, or identically $b$, or $\lambda\le\sum_{i:f_i=a}w_i\le1-\lambda$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extending a normalized noise bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_contraction_of_unit_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_normalization}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i>0$, $p>0$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Define $G(f)=\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p$ and $F(f)=\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2$. If $G(f)=1$ implies $F(f)\le1$ for every real vector $f$, then $F(f)\le G(f)^{2/p}$ for every $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp weighted finite-noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_sharp_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.exists_nonnegative_noise_maximizer, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_contraction_of_unit_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_maximizer_two_values, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_mass_dichotomy, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_two_value_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.weighted_two_point_le_of_atom_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{6}
Let $I$ be finite, let $\sum_iw_i=1$, let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and assume $w_i\ge\lambda$ for all $i$. Put $p=q/(q-1)$ and $\rho=\rho_*(q,\lambda)$. Every real vector $f$ satisfies $\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2\le(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p)^{2/p}$. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$.
\end{theorem}
